title: Benchmarking and Pushing the Multi-Bias Elimination Boundary of LLMs via Causal Effect Estimation-guided Debiasing

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating Natural Language Inference (NLI) model predictions on premise-hypothesis pairs constructed using templates that combine unisex names with statistically male-biased or female-biased occupations.
Evaluating NLI model predictions on premise-hypothesis pairs with artificially controlled high or low word overlap rates to see if models spuriously associate overlap with specific labels.
Evaluating NLI model predictions on premise-hypothesis pairs where the hypothesis is strictly controlled to be significantly shorter or longer than the premise (by more than five words).
Evaluating NLI model predictions on premise-hypothesis pairs engineered to have specific high or low BERTScore semantic similarities.

Evaluating NLI model predictions on premise-hypothesis pairs where specific speculative words (e.g., 'might', 'could', 'probably') are purposefully injected to test if the model associates them with specific inference labels.
